title: Most Used Phrasal Verbs
sub: Learn the meaning, then use it in a sentence.

examples: Find out when the train leaves.
I'll find out the price and call you back.
She found out about the surprise party.
We need to find out why the order failed.
She turned down the job offer.
Please turn down the TV; the baby is sleeping.
The bank turned down my loan application.
He turned down the offer because of the long commute.
He turned up an hour late.
Can you turn up the volume a little?
Only ten people turned up for the meeting.
My lost keys turned up in my coat pocket.

cards.def: To end a relationship; to split into pieces.
examples: They broke up last spring.
The band broke up after ten years together.
The meeting broke up at six.
Break up the big task into smaller steps.
They called off the match because of rain.
The company called off the strike after talks.
We called off the trip because my mother was ill.
The wedding was called off at the last minute.
I'm cutting down on sugar.
The doctor told him to cut down on salt.
We cut down our travel costs by using video calls.
Try to cut down your screen time before bed.

cards.def: To complete a form; to substitute.
examples: Please fill in this form.
Fill in your name and address in capital letters.
Can you fill in for me at the meeting tomorrow?
She filled in for the teacher who was on leave.
I get along well with my team.
My sister and I get along much better now.
Do you get along with your new neighbours?
It's easier to work in a team where people get along.
It took weeks to get over the flu.
She never got over losing her first job.
It took him months to get over the breakup.
You'll get over your fear of speaking with practice.
He finally gave in and agreed.
The child cried until his mother gave in.
Don't give in to pressure to sign quickly.
After a long argument, the landlord gave in.
What's going on here?
Please go on; I'm listening.
The meeting went on for three hours.
What's going on with the website today?
Hold on, I'll be right back.
Hold on to the handle when the bus moves.
Can you hold on a minute while I check?
Hold on, I think I left my phone in the cab.
Keep up the good work.
It's hard to keep up with all the new technology.
Walk slower; I can't keep up.
She reads the news daily to keep up with current events.
I don't want to let you down.
The weather let us down on our beach holiday.
He felt let down when his friend didn't come.
Please don't let the team down this time.
She looks after her grandmother.
Who will look after your dog while you travel?
Nurses look after patients day and night.
Look after yourself and get some rest.
I look forward to meeting you.
The kids look forward to summer holidays every year.
We look forward to working with you.
I'm looking forward to my first salary.

cards.def: To invent; to reconcile; to compensate.
examples: He made up an excuse.
The couple made up after a small fight.
He made up a story about a traffic jam.
I'll work late to make up for the time I lost.
I can't put up with the noise.
I can't put up with his rude comments anymore.
We put up with the old flat because it was cheap.
She puts up with a long commute for a good job.

cards.def: To leave the ground; to remove clothing; to become successful.
examples: The plane takes off at noon.
Take off your shoes before entering the temple.
Her online business really took off last year.
Our flight took off thirty minutes late.
Don't throw away the receipt.
We throw away too much food at weddings.
Don't throw away old clothes; donate them.
He threw away a great chance by arriving late.
Try out the new editor.
Try out the free version before you buy.
She tried out for the college cricket team.
We're trying out a new way to run stand-ups.
